newsitem.title: USA: TELKOM sees modest 96 revs per line growth.
newsitem.headline: TELKOM sees modest 96 revs per line growth.

text.p: PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia's (TELKOM) Director of Human Resources John Welly said the company expects revenue per line to grow modestly in 1996, despite a first half 1996 decrease of about 2.3 percent from last year's first half.
TELKOM, the leading provider of telecommunications services in Indonesia, experienced revenue per line growth of 4.4 percent from 1993 to 1995.

Speaking at the Asia '96 Flemings Conference in New York, Welly said that while it is very difficult to calculate future revenue per line growth, he said TELKOM "expects to increase revenues per line in the future."

Welly said TELKOM's growth in revenues per line was due to a number of factors, including a focus on marketing to business subscribers, and introduction of new value-added services, increasing incentives for subscribers to add lines, as well as an improvement in the network's technical quality.

Welly said 1996 first half net income increased to nearly 702 billion Indonesian rupiah, a 45 percent increase over 1995's first half. He said first half 1996 operating income also increased to about 946 billion rupiah.
TELKOM is in the process of reevaluating its long-term investment portfolio, Welly said. Key investment criteria under evaluation include strategic fit and profitability, he said.

Welly cited TELKOM's previously announced decision to decrease its ownership in its Ratelindo subsidiary as an example of its portfolio reevaluation. He said TELEKOM does not expect Ratelindo to earn a profit in the near future and said it no longer fits into the company's long term plans.
